_fixture.note: Hand-authored retrieval decision table for the lexical (FTS5/BM25) baseline. Every host is a reserved .invalid documentation name, so nothing here resolves or was captured from the internet. The documents are invented prose whose term distribution makes each expected order explainable; the fixture is a ranking rule, not a measurement of a live corpus.

documents.why: A body pass that contains both a query term and a distinctive partner term.
documents.body:
Espresso Brewing

Espresso is brewed by forcing hot water through finely ground coffee under pressure.

An espresso extraction usually finishes in about thirty seconds.

documents.why: Shares the term 'hot water' with other documents, so it can be crowded out.
documents.body:
Steeping

Tea is steeped in hot water, not brewed under pressure.

Green tea prefers cooler water.

documents.why: Holds far more 'water' passages than the diversity bound allows in one result.
documents.body:
Water Quality

Filtered water improves the taste of both coffee and tea.

Water that is too hot scalds the grounds.

documents.why: Holds the only passage that joins two uncommon query terms.
documents.body:
Pressure

Nine bars is a common espresso pressure.

Pressure drives the extraction, so weak coffee means weak pressure.

documents.why: Three body passages with identical length and term frequency, so their BM25 scores tie and the recorded ordinal rule decides.
The term is in the heading, so the recorded heading weight must rank it above body-only matches.

queries.why: Only one passage contains both 'filtered' and 'water'.
Only one passage contains both 'nine' and 'bars'.
'steeped' is a distinct token from the 'Steeping' heading, so only the body passage matches.

A heading match outranks body matches, and the three tied body matches fall back to ascending ordinal. The default per-source bound of two culls the third body match, which is why only ordinals 1 and 2 survive.

refusals.why: An empty query holds no term to retrieve.
A query of only whitespace is the same fact as an empty one.
A query of only punctuation reduces to no alphanumeric term.
A result limit below one cannot be honoured.
Resolution names a passage that was never indexed.
A result limit above the recorded policy maximum cannot be honoured, so the boundary refuses instead of silently returning fewer results than were asked for.
